elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence: "Company may terminate this Agreement or any Statement of Work for convenience upon thirty (30) days advance written notice to Contractor" — Statement of Work is this MSA's order-form analogue.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: "upon thirty (30) days advance written notice to Contractor" — exactly 30 days, in writing.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: "Contractor shall refund any prepaid fees pro rata for the period after the effective date of such termination" — express pro-rata basis, not merely a post-termination-period refund.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: "Contractor may not terminate this Agreement or any Statement of Work for convenience while any Statement of Work is outstanding." Retained § 6(a) 15-day mutual right is expressly available only when no SOW is outstanding, so the two are mutually exclusive; in this indefinite MSA the period of commitment is the pendency of a SOW.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The added right runs on 30 days' notice, not 60–90; no 60–90 day mechanic appears anywhere.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no early-termination fee or penalty exists in the retained or added language (only earned fees through the effective date under § 6(b)), so there is nothing to cap.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Retained § 6(a) lets Contractor terminate on 15 days' notice whenever no SOW is outstanding; that effective date is not tied to the end of any then-current term, and the indefinite term has no end anchor.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Contractor's surviving § 6(a) convenience right requires only fifteen (15) days advance notice.

reasons: Preferred level is complete: the inserted sentence supplies the Customer convenience right over both the Agreement and any Statement of Work, a 30-day written-notice trigger, an express pro-rata prepaid-fee refund, and a bar on Contractor convenience termination while any SOW is outstanding.

The Vendor-bar element is satisfied in substance because retained § 6(a) is self-limited to periods with no uncompleted Statement of Work, so no contradiction arises with the new prohibition; the mutual 15-day gap-period right is Customer-favourable and correctly retained.

Fallback is incomplete (30-day notice rather than 60–90; Contractor's 15-day gap right is not term-end anchored and is under 90 days), but that is immaterial because the proposal targets and completes the preferred level.

Minimal: a single concise insertion; §§ 2, 6(a) and 6(b) are reproduced verbatim with no deletions, no survival tail, no expense or damages add-ons, and no procedural extras. "In whole or in part" from the model language was correctly omitted as surplus.

Preserves intent: the § 6(b) breach mechanic, Contractor's earned-fee entitlement, the Works-in-progress assignment, and the § 2 cross-reference to Paragraph 6 all survive without contradiction or dangling references.
